paragraphs: “Why does this keep happening?” Help for Me (2021)

You may find yourself stuck and unexplainably returning to pornography again and again. Maybe you have tried different solutions. You may even experience progress for a time, but somehow you find yourself returning to pornography.

Being honest with yourself and others about your pornography use will help you make progress on your journey to change. One way to do this is to think carefully about your triggers. A trigger is something that creates a need or desire for you to seek out pornography. For example, some people feel triggered to view pornography after having experiences where they feel dismissed, unimportant, or unloved.

Take a few minutes to think about and write down triggers that may have led you to seek out pornography in the past. You can add to your list as more ideas come to you. Some examples of triggers include:
Post-traumatic stress or remembering past instances of abuse

When you feel ready, review each trigger you’ve written down. Can you connect this trigger to a specific instance in the past where you turned to pornography for comfort or distraction? Can you recognize any patterns in your past behavior? If you are in a similar situation again, what could you do differently? For example, instead of turning to pornography, is there a trusted friend, family member, or counselor you could contact? You could talk to him or her about how you’re feeling, or you could just engage in small talk. Other ideas include physical activity, listening to music, writing in a journal or reading a book, or providing service for someone else.

This process can be a step toward freeing yourself from behaviors that defined you in the past. In the past, you may not have thought about when and why you turned to pornography. You may have justified your behavior or blamed other people, places, or things. But now you can begin to take responsibility for your actions, even though you may need to acknowledge painful, embarrassing, or difficult events. Being honest with yourself and others about your pornography use will also open your heart to receiving help from your Father in Heaven and the Savior and will prepare you to discover insights that will lead toward repentance and healing.
Examine some of the thoughts you have about yourself. Which of these thoughts align with gospel truths? Which of these thoughts may not be true at all?
Discuss healthy sexual behavior with your spouse, parents, or an appropriate support person. It may also be helpful to talk with a mental health or medical professional who shares your values.

If you’re married, talk with your spouse about what he or she is experiencing as a result of your pornography use. It can be important and useful for you and your spouse to share how you are both feeling.

Life has many challenges, and sometimes we need extra support to face them. Learn more below about Church resources like Family Services and how to recognize whether counseling or other support options are right for you.
Professional counseling is not always necessary to deal with mental, emotional, or relational difficulties. Depending on the situation, self-help resources can be sufficient.

However, when challenges interfere significantly with relationships, the ability to accomplish daily tasks, or both, or when they result in ongoing distress or feelings of hopelessness, professional counseling can be an important way to learn more effective ways to cope.
See When to Consider Professional Help for a more specific list of mental health issues that could benefit from counseling.

Counseling cannot fix everything in life or result in clients having perfect mental and emotional health. Only through Christ is that possible after this life. Counseling can help you make strides in facing, growing through, and even overcoming many challenges in your life.

To benefit the most from counseling, you must fully engage in the process and be willing to make changes. Ensure you take responsibility for your own mental health by doing the following during the counseling process:

After you receive a referral to Family Services from your bishop or branch president, you may be asked to schedule an initial discussion with a Family Services counselor. During the consultation, you will have the opportunity to explain what help you’re looking for.

The Family Services staff member will discuss with you different options to address your concerns. This could include anything from self-help materials, professional counseling, or referrals to community resources.

Family Services offers group therapy for specific concerns as well as short-term counseling (generally up to 12 sessions) for individuals, couples, and families. Counseling may be provided virtually or in person.
Members who have mental health insurance coverage or other resources, or who have needs outside of Family Services scope of services, may be guided in using community resources.

Group therapy has been shown to be an invaluable part of treatment for many participants. While group members may initially feel unsure about discussing challenges in a group setting, they often find that they gain beneficial insights from fellow group members and come to feel a sense of connection as they develop valuable tools and skills.

Medications can help manage certain mental health conditions. Typically, they are most effective when combined with counseling that focuses on developing healthy coping skills.

Medications are not always needed for mental health problems. Care and discretion should be used when seeking advice regarding medications from medical providers.

Engaging in activities that keep you connected to our Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ is an important way to maintain good mental and emotional health. Our relationship with Them can increase a sense of purpose and meaning and can contribute to resilience during times of difficulty. We are promised that we can find strength as we connect ourselves to Jesus Christ. Participating in church can also connect you with a community that can help provide support and resources.

If you are concerned about your mental health, it can be helpful to ponder and make a personal record of your involvement in activities that build your relationship with Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ, including Church and temple worship, scripture study, prayer, and service.
